pride_data.title: Site-Link for identification of chromatinized proteome defined by site-specific histone acylations in living cells
pride_data.projectDescription: By coupling the mass spectrometry, we developed the Site-Link strategy based on the GCE method for analyzing the interacting proteome of histone lysine acylations in living cells. As K* could mimic the natural lysine to be recognized by natural lysine synthase, histones bearing the site-specifically incorporated K*acyl, should also be also integrated into nucleosomes and further compacted into chromatin similar as Kacyl with cell passaging. The subsequent 365-nm light irradiation could activate the diazirine and covalently capture potential effector proteins on native chromatin in living cells. The effector proteins could be identified after gel-based proteomics and MS/MS analysis of the crosslinked histone-effector complexes.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Plasmids pcDNA4-H3-K37TAG (C-terminal myc-His-tag) or pcDNA4-H3-K56TAG (C-terminal myc-His-tag) was transfected into the relative PylRS stable cell line and supplemented with 0.2 mM K*cr/K*ac/PABK*. After growing for 6 h, the transfected HEK293T cells were changed into DMEM with 1mM K*cr/K*bhb/PABK*. The cells were cultured for additional 36 hours to express the corresponding H3 protein (H3K*56ac/H3K*37cr). The cells were cultured for additional 24 hours, followed by addition of TCO (0.5 mM) to decage the PAB group  to express the corresponding H3 protein (H3K*56PABK*). The medium was discarded and Dulbecco’s phosphate buffered saline (DPBS) was added. After ultraviolet irradiation of the cells on ice for 15 min, cells were harvested. The histones were extracted by TCA precipitation and enriched by his-tag isolation. The eluents were combined, concentrated, and separated by SDS-PAGE. The crosslinked bands and the relative bands without UV irradiation were cut for subjected to HPLC-MS/MS proteomic study.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The raw files were searched against Human fasta database (20,361 sequences) (downloaded from Uniprot on July 1st, 2018) by MaxQuant (version 1.6.1.0). with the following parameters: The carbamidomethyl (Cys) was set as the fixed modification, while oxidation (Met) was set as variable modification. +/- 10 ppm was set for peptide pass tolerance and +/- 0.6 Da was set for fragment mass tolerance. A maximum of two missed cleavages was allowed for trypsin digestion. FDR was determined by searching a reverse database and was set to 0.01 for proteins and peptides. Proteins with spectral counts no less than 2 were recognized as possible candidates after Maxquant searching.
